functions.name: Research attention
functions.detail: Which tickers opted-in Gloom users are researching, by hour, day and week, with sector and country totals and abnormal attention. Delayed at least an hour. Pro shows the full board; Free shows three rows per section.

functions.name: Security overview
functions.detail: The starting point for any ticker: live quote, day and 52-week range, price chart, fundamentals, and tabs into every other research pane. T is the same pane; search Ticker Research to open a second one.

functions.name: Quote monitor
functions.detail: A compact board of live quotes for any list of tickers, each with change, range, and a sparkline. Good as the always-open strip in a layout.

functions.name: Price chart
functions.detail: A price chart with volume in the chart composer, defaulting to a multi-year range. Add indicators, drawings, or other series from the same pane.

functions.name: Intraday chart
functions.detail: One or five sessions of intraday candles with the session boundaries marked. Real-time on Pro, 15-minute delayed on Free.

functions.name: Time and sales
functions.detail: Recent prints from the consolidated tape with time, price, size, venue, and conditions; prints of 10,000 shares or more stand out. US equities, real-time on Pro, 15-minute delayed on Free.

functions.name: Quote recap
functions.detail: NBBO history: bid and ask with sizes, venues, and spread in basis points, plus the median and widest spread and locked or crossed quotes. The NBBO tab of TAS.

functions.name: Custom chart
functions.detail: The chart composer with an explicit series list: prices, statement lines, valuation multiples, FRED series, indicators, and formulas on shared or separate axes. Series read SYMBOL:field or FRED:series, as in NVDA:price, FRED:CPIAUCSL; start empty to search the catalog.

functions.name: Data catalog
functions.detail: Searches every series the chart composer knows: securities, options, crypto, FRED, treasuries, and futures. Pick one to chart it.

functions.name: Financial analysis
functions.detail: Annual and quarterly statements with the line items you expect, plus derived margins and growth. Switch periods and statements with the tabs.

functions.name: Credit documents
functions.detail: Instrument balances, maturities, covenants, change-of-control terms and amendment history with primary-document evidence. Pro includes the full dataset; free access previews three instruments.

functions.name: Covenants
functions.detail: Maintenance tests and disclosed financial metrics, with headroom only when contractual definitions and borrower scope match. Screen for low headroom and upcoming springing maturities.

functions.name: Debt maturities
functions.detail: Principal due in the next 12 months, in each of years two to five, and after, from the latest annual filing, with the near-term share ranked against 10 years. History tracks principal and interest expense.

functions.name: Historical prices
functions.detail: Daily open, high, low, close, and volume in a scrollable table, exportable to CSV from pane settings.

functions.name: Compare performance
functions.detail: Price returns rebased to a shared start date for two or more tickers, so relative performance is readable at a glance.

functions.name: Fundamental graph
functions.detail: Quarterly revenue for one or more companies as grouped columns, with any other statement field one click away in the series editor.

functions.name: Valuation graph
functions.detail: Trailing P/E history for one or more tickers; switch to forward P/E, PEG, P/S, EV/EBITDA, or P/FCF in the series editor.

functions.name: Relationship graph
functions.detail: How two tickers move together: indexed prices, their ratio, rolling correlation, and a return regression with beta, alpha, and R².

functions.name: Correlation matrix
functions.detail: A date-aligned Pearson correlation matrix of daily returns for a basket, useful for checking how diversified a set of names really is.

functions.name: Backtest
functions.detail: Tests a long-only rule on daily history against buy-and-hold: a preset like golden cross or RSI, or your own, like rsi(14) < 30. Equity and drawdown curves, CAGR, Sharpe, and every trade. BTST opens it too.

functions.name: Relative valuation
functions.detail: Valuation and operating metrics for a peer group in one table: market cap, P/E, EV/EBITDA, margins, growth, and more.

functions.name: Equity screener
functions.detail: Filter covered stocks on valuation, growth, margins, liquidity, short interest, insider activity, and 13F holders, then rank the matches by any metric. Exports to CSV; saving a screen needs a verified email.

functions.name: Options monitor
functions.detail: Calls and puts by expiry with bid, ask, volume, open interest, implied volatility, and Greeks. Real-time on Pro.

functions.name: Options positioning
functions.detail: Open interest by strike with max pain, each expiry's put/call ratio and net dealer gamma, and dealer gamma by strike with its flip level and call and put walls. Open interest is about two sessions old; the footer names its date. GEX and MAXPAIN open it too.

functions.name: Options calculator
functions.detail: Price a European call or put from spot, strike, rate, volatility, and expiry, or solve for implied volatility from a market price.

functions.name: Options scenario
functions.detail: Build a multi-leg options position from the chain, from OMON, or by hand, and value it at any spot, date, and vol shift: payoff, P&L grid, breakevens, and Greeks. European pricing, so no early exercise.

functions.name: Volatility surface
functions.detail: The implied volatility surface fitted from option quotes: 3D sheet, table, smiles, ATM term structure, 25-delta skew, and forwards. Steps back through stored daily closes; live is real-time on Pro, 15-minute delayed on Free.

functions.name: Implied volatility history
functions.detail: Daily 30- and 90-day at-the-money implied vol since February 2024 against realized vol, with the spread and each measure's 52-week rank and percentile. A new ticker backfills in a few minutes.

functions.name: Realized volatility
functions.detail: Rolling realized volatility over windows from 10 to 260 sessions, with price and today's at-the-money IV for reference. Five estimators, from close-to-close to Yang-Zhang.

functions.name: Volatility cone
functions.detail: Each window's realized volatility against its one- or two-year range, as a cone and a table, with today's at-the-money IV on top: is vol high for this name? The Cone tab of HVG.

functions.name: Seasonality
functions.detail: Monthly returns for each year as a heatmap, every month's average, median and share of up years, each year's path laid over one January-to-December axis, and a Weekdays tab with the average return, up share and session count for each weekday and the turn of the month.

functions.name: Volatility rich/cheap
functions.detail: IV rank, term slope, skew, and IV against realized vol for up to 60 US tickers, flagged rich or cheap against each name's own year. Without tickers it screens index and sector ETFs.

functions.name: Analyst research
functions.detail: Consensus price target with the range, the rating distribution, and recent upgrades, downgrades, and initiations by firm.

functions.name: Earnings estimates
functions.detail: Quarterly and annual EPS and revenue estimates next to reported results, with beats and misses.

functions.name: Estimate revisions
functions.detail: Consensus EPS by quarter and year with its latest change, 30-day up and down revisions, and range; open a period to chart it. Surprises and Guidance tabs too. EEO opens it too.

functions.name: Company KPIs
functions.detail: Company-reported operating metrics by fiscal period, with native currencies, definitions, charts, source quotes and retained restatements. Three latest series are free to preview; full history is Pro.

functions.name: Guidance tracker
functions.detail: Management guidance as dated ranges and points, with raises, cuts, withdrawals and later actuals when the period and accounting basis match. Cited evidence and revision history. Three current guides are free to preview; full coverage is Pro.

functions.name: Company guidance
functions.detail: The outlook the company gave on its latest earnings call, pulled from the transcript, above consensus for the coming periods. US listings. The Guidance tab of EM.

functions.name: Corporate actions
functions.detail: Dividend and split history plus past and upcoming earnings dates and estimates in one timeline.

functions.name: Dividend yield
functions.detail: Cash distributions, trailing yield, indicated rate when available, and payout growth. Future payments are not forecast.

functions.name: Short interest
functions.detail: Bi-monthly FINRA settlement data with shares short, days to cover, and average daily volume over time.

functions.name: Daily short volume
functions.detail: FINRA daily off-exchange short volume as a share of volume, charted against its one-year range. Not short interest; SI has that.

functions.name: Equity diagnostic
functions.detail: A read of the company's filings and numbers into red flags, anomalies, green flags, and items to watch, each with the evidence it came from.

functions.name: Risk factors
functions.detail: The 10-K risk factor section grouped by theme, with the items that were added, dropped, or rewritten since the prior year called out.

functions.name: Executives
functions.description: Officers and pay from the proxy
functions.detail: Named executive officers and their compensation, read from the proxy statement and checked against the filing.

functions.name: 8-K filings
functions.detail: The company's 8-Ks classified by item (agreements, executive changes, auditor changes, restructurings) with a summary of what each one said.

functions.name: Earnings calls
functions.detail: Earnings call transcripts with speaker attribution, the analyst Q&A, and extracted guidance and notable quotes. Without a ticker it lists every transcribed call as they land.

functions.name: Hiring momentum
functions.detail: Weekly open roles, role and location mix, remote share, hiring changes and peers for one company. Pro shows the full history; Free shows the latest values and three rows per section.

functions.name: App attention
functions.description: App ranks, ratings and company momentum
functions.detail: Public app chart ranks by storefront, matched rank velocity, rating drift, country spreads and listed-parent comparisons. Open an app for its rank history.

functions.name: Hiring
functions.description: Open roles, by function, over time
functions.detail: Open roles read daily from a company's own careers site: trend, function, country, seniority, new roles, pay ranges and themes such as AI. Without a ticker it ranks every covered company.

functions.name: Research search
functions.detail: Full-text search across earnings call transcripts, news wires, and SEC filings, with the matching passage inline. Save a search to get alerted on new hits.

functions.name: AI screener
functions.detail: Describe a screen in plain language and get a table of matching tickers, saved as a reusable tab. Uses the AI provider you configure.

functions.name: AI agent
functions.detail: A long-running AI thread with your choice of model that can read your panes and run research commands for you.

functions.name: Ask Gloom
functions.detail: Ask a question about what is on screen and watch the tools Gloom runs to answer it. Requires a verified Cloud account.

functions.name: Top news
functions.detail: Curated stories ranked by importance across wires, publishers, and X, with tickers and category. The pane to keep open when you only want what matters.

functions.name: News feed
functions.detail: Every story as it arrives, newest first, with source, tickers, sentiment, and importance score; filter by sentiment or minimum score. Add News Feed adds your own RSS feed (desktop and terminal, not web).

functions.name: Ticker news
functions.detail: Stories linked to the selected ticker, newest first.

functions.name: Topic news
functions.description: News by topic code or sector
functions.detail: Market news by topic code (MNA, CB, ENERGY, REG, CRYPTO, EARN, IPO) or by sector. LTR lists public fund and investor letters as links to the publisher's page.

functions.name: Breaking news
functions.detail: Stories flagged as breaking or urgent. Turn on Notifications in its pane settings to hear about new ones even while the pane is closed.

functions.name: X feed
functions.detail: An X advanced-search feed for any ticker or query with likes and views, refreshed live. Needs a verified email.

functions.name: Social mentions
functions.description: Daily X posts naming a cashtag
functions.detail: Daily posts on X naming the ticker's cashtag, the day's top posts and their stance.

functions.name: Substack
functions.detail: Your Substack subscriptions as a reader feed inside the terminal, signed in with your own account.

functions.name: Live TV
functions.detail: Live financial television in a pane (desktop and terminal with a capable renderer).

functions.name: Hacker News
functions.detail: Top, New, Best, Show, and Ask with scores and comment counts. Also the reference plugin if you want to write your own.

functions.name: Market movers
functions.detail: Today's top gainers, losers, most active and trending tickers with price, change, volume against average and market cap. Pro adds pre-market and after-hours movers and the gaps at the open.

functions.name: World equity indices
functions.detail: Major indices grouped by region with last, change, and session status, so you can see which markets are open and how they closed.

functions.name: Sector performance
functions.detail: S&P 500 sectors and industries sorted by the day's move, with their representative ETFs.

functions.name: Index and ETF members
functions.description: ETF holdings, member returns and index changes
functions.detail: IVV, IJH, IJR, IWM and IWB holdings with weights, member returns, daily contributions and index changes. SPX and SPY use IVV holdings.

functions.name: Relative rotation
functions.detail: Each name's strength against SPY or another benchmark, plotted against its momentum with weekly trails through the four quadrants. Sector ETFs by default, or your tickers. GRR opens it too.

functions.name: Market heatmap
functions.detail: The 500 largest US stocks grouped by sector and industry, or the largest ETFs, as a treemap colored by the day's move and moving with live quotes. Sized by the square root of market cap, or by market cap itself.

functions.name: FX cross rates
functions.detail: A cross-rate matrix for the major currencies, updated live.

functions.name: Crypto board
functions.detail: The top 100 coins by market cap, stablecoins on their own tab, with returns from a day to a year, a 30-day sparkline, volume, and market cap. Prices stream live on every plan where the market allows.

functions.name: Perpetual history
functions.description: Funding, open interest and premium history
functions.detail: Funding, open interest and premium history for one perpetual on Hyperliquid, Binance, Bybit or OKX, with each reading's source. Pro shows the history; Free a limited preview. Live board and trading are in the Hyperliquid plugin.

functions.name: Futures board
functions.detail: Each root's most active contract across equity index, rates, energy, metals, agriculture, and FX with last price, unit and session change, grouped by sector, naming the nearer month while it still trades.

functions.name: Futures curve
functions.detail: A futures root's listed contracts as a curve against a week and a month ago, with roll yield, contango or backwardation, and each contract's price, open interest, and volume.

functions.name: Fear and greed
functions.detail: The CNN Fear & Greed index with its history and each of the seven component indicators.

functions.name: CFTC positioning
functions.detail: Weekly CFTC Commitments of Traders: net positioning by trader class, the weekly change, and one- and three-year percentiles. Pass a root like CL to chart it under the front-month price. CFTC opens it too.

functions.name: Power and grid buildout
functions.detail: Grid interconnection queues, datacentre and other large-load requests, generation capacity and utility exposure, with a link to the source for every project. Pro shows the full data and history; Free shows three rows per section. EPWR opens the Prices tab, free: day-ahead power prices for 32 European markets in EUR/MWh and the EU carbon (EUA) auction clearing price in EUR/tCO2, each with its daily history. EPWR GAS shows European gas storage from GIE AGSI+: % full, TWh and daily injection and withdrawal for the EU and each member state, against a year ago and the five-year range.

functions.name: Exposure engine
functions.detail: Apply country, supplier, customer, tariff, commodity, rate and FX shocks to holdings and see exposure ranges and the paths behind them. Free previews one holding and one hop; Pro covers 100 holdings and four hops.

functions.name: GPU Rental Prices
functions.detail: What it costs to rent a GPU by the hour: published prices, spot rates and marketplace asks in USD per GPU-hour, with history and related equities. Pro shows the full board; Free shows the three latest rows.

functions.name: Government awards
functions.detail: Government awards, subcontractors and modifications with verified company matches, native-currency amounts, agency concentration, sector rankings, cumulative obligations and primary-source evidence. Pro includes filters and history; everyone can view a three-row preview.

functions.name: Revenue breakdown
functions.detail: Quarterly revenue by product, segment or region from the company's 10-Q and 10-K filings. Free shows the first two lines; Pro shows every line.

functions.name: Reverse DCF
functions.detail: The yearly free cash flow growth over ten years that makes a DCF equal today's enterprise value, next to the growth the company actually delivered.

functions.name: P/E band
functions.detail: Weekly price against round multiples of trailing EPS, stepping when each EPS figure became known, with today's P/E ranked in the stock's own history.

functions.name: Returns
functions.detail: Interval and cumulative price returns in a scrollable table, for a range and granularity you pick.

functions.name: Macro-day reaction
functions.description: How a name moves on CPI, jobs, FOMC
functions.detail: A name's average move on CPI, jobs report and FOMC days against a normal day, with the share of up days and the move on every release day.

functions.name: Short squeeze watch
functions.description: Crowded shorts that are moving up
functions.detail: Short interest as a share of float, days to cover, the change since the prior settlement and the month's price move across your portfolios and watchlists, or the tickers you give. Updates twice a month.

functions.name: Earnings ripple
functions.description: Holdings tied to a company reporting soon
functions.detail: Customers your holdings name in their filings, and suppliers whose filings name your holdings, with the disclosed revenue share, by report date.

functions.name: Supply chain
functions.detail: Who a company buys from and sells to, with the filing, call or announcement behind each link: Table, Flow, Graph and Path views, up to four hops. Free previews three relationships per role; Pro shows everything.

functions.name: Catalysts
functions.detail: A calendar of regulatory, clinical, legal and trade-policy events linked to companies, with source documents and every revision. Free previews three events; Pro shows them all, with alerts.

functions.name: Litigation
functions.detail: One company's litigation, enforcement and antitrust cases, with primary documents and dated status changes. Free previews three events; Pro shows them all.

functions.name: Clinical trials
functions.description: Studies by condition, drug or sponsor
functions.detail: Clinical studies by condition, drug or sponsor, with status, phase and enrollment. Open a study for its full record.

functions.name: FDA reports
functions.detail: FDA drug and device adverse event reports and drug recalls, by drug, device or firm name. A report is what someone observed, not proof the product caused it.

functions.name: Oil and gas inventories
functions.detail: The EIA's weekly oil and natural gas storage: crude, Cushing, the SPR, products and gas by region, each with the week's build or draw and its place in the five-year range. NGS opens the gas tab.

functions.name: VIX term structure
functions.detail: Daily 30-day and three-month VIX closes from FRED, so you can see whether the curve is in contango or inverted.

functions.name: Cross-asset volatility
functions.detail: Volatility indices across assets on one board: the VIX term, VVIX, SKEW, MOVE, and index, commodity, and emerging-market vol, each with its one-year percentile. The Cross-asset tab of VIX.

functions.name: New highs and lows
functions.detail: A live count of stocks printing new session highs and lows over 30-second, one-minute, and five-minute windows. Real-time on Pro, 15-minute delayed on Free.

functions.name: Options flow
functions.detail: Sweeps, blocks, and large premium prints as they hit the tape, with ticker, strike, expiry, and premium.

functions.name: Market halts
functions.detail: Current and recent US trading halts with the reason code and resumption times.

functions.name: IPO calendar
functions.detail: Upcoming and recently listed IPOs worldwide, with price in local currency, deal size in dollars, and first-day return.

functions.name: Thematic baskets
functions.detail: Curated themes with equal-weight returns and breadth. Open a theme for its members, leaders and laggards. The Themes tab of BI.

functions.name: M&A
functions.detail: Pending, rumored and closed mergers and acquisitions, with arbitrage spreads on listed targets. Free is delayed 7 days; Pro is live.

functions.name: Distress
functions.detail: Dated public records about companies in difficulty: 8-K bankruptcy, obligation and listing filings, SEC going-concern disclosures, Taiwan exchange listing designations, and French and UK insolvency notices. The Distress tab of MA.

functions.name: World venue map
functions.detail: Trading venues around the world with open or closed status, local time, and time to the next session change.

functions.name: Prediction markets
functions.detail: Browse and search Polymarket and Kalshi markets by category with top odds, spread, and volume, and chart any market's history.

functions.name: Polls
functions.detail: VoteHub polls by type (approval, favorability, generic ballot, Senate, governor, House) with trend charts and pollster breakdowns.

functions.name: Chokepoint transits
functions.detail: Daily vessel transits through the main shipping chokepoints, charted together or one by name. Use it to see a disruption in trade before it shows up in prices; each transit series also charts in G next to oil or a shipper.

functions.name: Economic calendar
functions.detail: Upcoming releases and central bank events with impact, country, actual, forecast, and prior.

functions.name: Economic statistics
functions.detail: Inflation, labour, growth, housing, and rates indicators with the latest print, the prior, and a chart against their own history.

functions.name: US consumer prices
functions.detail: US inflation by component (food, energy, core goods, shelter, services ex shelter) with each one's weight, monthly and yearly change, and points added to the headline. The header gives the next release. ECAN opens it too.

functions.name: Central bank rates
functions.detail: Policy rates for the G20 central banks, the SNB, Norges Bank, the Riksbank and the RBNZ with the last move, its date, and a one-year percentile; open one for its history. ECFC and CBRT open it too.

functions.name: Yield curves
functions.detail: Government yield curves: US Treasury, TIPS real yields and breakevens, euro AAA, Bund, Gilt, JGB and Canada, with spreads like 2s10s and their one-year percentiles, a two-date difference and a World tab. GC JGB opens a curve directly.

functions.name: US rate path
functions.detail: The fed funds rate priced for each upcoming FOMC meeting from futures, against a week and a month ago and the Fed's projections, with per-meeting probabilities. FFIP opens it too.

functions.name: Credit spreads
functions.detail: ICE BofA US corporate option-adjusted spreads by rating bucket and high yield, with the day's change.

functions.name: Treasury auctions
functions.detail: Bill, note, bond, and TIPS auction results from the US Treasury: high rate, bid-to-cover, indirect share, and size.

functions.name: Money markets
functions.detail: Funding rates (SOFR, EFFR, IORB), Treasury bill yields and their curve, and Fed liquidity from reserves to the reverse repo, each with its one-year percentile and history.

functions.name: Single-name CDS
functions.detail: Single-name corporate CDS. CDS alone lists the issuers traded in the last 5 days with trade count, last trade and 5Y spread, to rank them by; with a ticker or issuer, its 5Y spread (level, date, 1M change, range) and its trades.

functions.name: Index CDS
functions.description: CDX and iTraxx on the run
functions.detail: CDX IG, HY and EM with iTraxx Main and Crossover on the run: the 5Y level, 1D and 1W moves, 1Y percentile and the day's print count. IG and iTraxx in spread, HY and EM in price.

functions.name: Sovereign CDS
functions.detail: Sovereign 5Y CDS ranked by the month's move, beside the local currency's move against the dollar, with each country's year of history. WCDS opens it too.

functions.name: Bond calculator
functions.detail: Price a fixed-coupon bond from a yield, or solve the yield from a price: accrued interest, duration, convexity, DV01, spread to Treasuries, cash flows, and price at yield shifts.

functions.name: Fixed Income
functions.detail: One workspace for credit markets, issuer debt, corporate bond sales, Treasury auctions, Treasury cash and debt, and primary dealer positions. FI opens it; the older shortcuts still land on their own section.

functions.name: Corporate bond tape
functions.detail: Latest corporate and agency bond sales: issuer, coupon, price, yield, and grade. TRACE alone lists the tape; TRACE with an issuer filters to that name. It opens the Bonds section of Fixed Income.

functions.name: Treasury cash and debt
functions.description: Operating cash and debt held by the public
functions.detail: Treasury operating cash for the latest day, and debt held by the public for the last 20 business days. It opens the Treasury section of Fixed Income.

functions.name: Primary dealer positions
functions.detail: Weekly net positions and settlement fails in Treasuries and mortgage-backed securities, from the primary dealers. It opens the Treasury section of Fixed Income.

functions.name: Market valuation
functions.detail: Market-wide valuation ratios against their own history, with zones and trend deviation.

functions.name: Earnings calendar
functions.detail: Upcoming earnings dates and estimates grouped by when they report, with implied and past moves. Alone it follows your portfolio and watchlists; with tickers, just those. EVTS opens it too.

functions.name: SEC filings
functions.detail: Recent SEC filings for a ticker with form type and date; open any of them inline. US equities only.

functions.name: Holders
functions.detail: Institutional holders as a table (value, shares, change, percent held) or as an ownership treemap.

functions.name: 13F funds
functions.detail: Browse institutional 13F filings by fund, ticker, or CIK with estimated long-book performance, holdings, and filing history. Option values are underlying notional, not market value.

functions.name: Insider transactions
functions.detail: Insider buys, sells, awards, and gifts from Form 4 filings with insider name, size, and price. Alone it ranks the companies whose insiders are buying in the market, with why: clusters, repeat buys, size against their usual. US equities only.

functions.name: Congress trades
functions.detail: Newly disclosed House and Senate periodic transaction reports: member, ticker, side, amount band, and filing lag, with a Chamber filter. Returns are hindsight price moves, not execution returns.

functions.name: ETF filings
functions.detail: A US-listed fund's SEC filings: registration statements, prospectus updates, shareholder reports, N-CEN and N-PORT reports. Open any of them inline.

functions.name: SEC comment letters
functions.detail: SEC staff comment letters and company responses, newest first. Search their text, or type a ticker for one company's letters.

functions.name: Portfolio
functions.detail: Your portfolio or watchlist with live quotes, P&L, weights, and sparklines. Set target weights and each holding shows its drift from them and the trade that rebalances it. Broker-synced and manual positions sit in the same table.

functions.name: Portfolio analytics
functions.detail: Opens on Risk depth: benchmark-relative risk, factor betas, and index, rate, and VIX stress shifts. The Overview view in pane settings has P&L, Sharpe, beta to the S&P 500, and sector allocation. MARS opens it too.

functions.name: Position sizer
functions.detail: Kelly-based position sizing for a ticker against your bankroll, with loss caps, expected growth, and the trim or add needed.

functions.name: Add to watchlist
functions.detail: Adds a ticker to the active watchlist.

functions.name: Add to portfolio
functions.detail: Adds a ticker to a manual portfolio, with optional shares, average cost, and currency. Search Set Portfolio Position to change a position later.

functions.name: Remove from watchlist
functions.detail: Removes a ticker from the active watchlist.

functions.name: Remove from portfolio
functions.detail: Removes a ticker and its positions from the active portfolio.

functions.name: Price alerts
functions.detail: Your price alerts with current price, distance to target, and trigger state.

functions.name: Add alert
functions.detail: Creates an alert from a symbol, a condition (above, below, crosses, or >, <, x), and a target price.

functions.name: Notes
functions.detail: A general-purpose notes pane. Ticker notes live in the research pane; this one is for anything else.

functions.name: Investment theses
functions.detail: Your theses and your teams', those needing a ruling first: kill conditions, catalysts, and conviction against position size. THESIS NVDA opens or starts one; on Pro it drafts the thesis and watches news and filings.

functions.name: Custom view
functions.detail: A table built from any data function, like MOST or RV, with your own columns, filters, and sort. Ask Gloom writes the spec or you paste the JSON; publish it to a team.

functions.name: Chat
functions.detail: Channels for equities, options, macro, crypto, and more, with replies and mentions. Opens the preferred channel or a named one.

functions.name: Direct messages
functions.detail: Opens an existing DM or starts a direct or group conversation by username.

functions.name: Teams
functions.detail: Members, invites, channels, and settings for your teams, which share layouts, lists, notes, theses, views, and chat. TEAM new creates one (Pro; joining is free); TEAM invite @user adds people.

functions.name: Team focus
functions.detail: Narrows the workspace to one team, personal only, or everything: other tabs fold away and new notes and lists default to the focus. Shown once you are in a team.

functions.name: TheBuildout
functions.detail: Data center and semiconductor supply chain intelligence from TheBuildout: company lists, sites, and intel. Limited free data; full access with a TheBuildout subscription.

functions.name: Account management
functions.detail: Profile, emails, Pro plan, teams, and password settings for your Gloom Cloud account.

functions.name: Upgrade to Pro
functions.detail: Opens Pro checkout, or the billing portal during a trial; signs you up first when signed out. Hidden once you pay for Pro; manage the plan in ACM.

functions.name: Brokers
functions.detail: Broker profiles, account sync, and connection status. Every broker (IBKR, Public, Robinhood, SimpleFIN) is a plugin you install first.

functions.name: IBKR trading
functions.detail: Live IBKR market data, a trading console and order entry through Gateway or TWS, in the terminal and desktop app only. Open Trading, Buy Selected and Sell Selected prefill a ticket. Orders hit your real account.

functions.name: Tidy windows
functions.detail: Arranges every open window into one tiled layout.

functions.name: Layouts
functions.detail: Browse saved and published layouts, switch between them, or add one to your workspace.

functions.name: Trading desks
functions.detail: Adds a ready-made desk as a new layout tab: equities, options, futures and commodities, rates and credit, FX and macro, or active trading. Also offered on first run, as 'What do you trade?'.

functions.name: Layout actions
functions.detail: Float, dock, swap, remove, and save panes and layouts.

functions.name: Window mode
functions.detail: Moves or resizes the focused window from the keyboard, for terminals where the mouse is not an option.

pages.title: Install Gloomberb: Mac, Windows, Linux, TUI
pages.lead: Install the Gloomberb desktop app on Mac or Windows, or run it in a terminal with one command. Then update it and confirm it runs.

blocks.text: macOS
Either command installs the desktop app and the `gloomberb` terminal command.

blocks.code:
brew install --cask gloomberb
# or
curl -fsSL gloom.sh/install | bash

blocks.text: Or use the [direct download](/download/desktop).

The desktop app and Homebrew cask require Apple Silicon. Intel Macs can use the [browser version](#browser); check [release assets](https://github.com/gloom-sh/gloomberb/releases/latest) for terminal binary availability.
Coming from Bloomberg? [What runs on a Mac](/answers/bloomberg-terminal-on-mac).
Linux
Terminal UI only; Ghostty, Kitty, or WezTerm render charts best. Installs `gloomberb` into `~/.local/bin`.

blocks.code: curl -fsSL gloom.sh/install | bash

blocks.text: Windows
The [desktop installer](/download/desktop), about 280 MB, installs the app and the `gloomberb` command for your user, with no admin rights. It is not code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may stop it:

items: Run the installer.
If Windows says "Windows protected your PC", click **More info**.
Click **Run anyway**.

blocks.text: To check the file first, compare `Get-FileHash` on it with the SHA-256 on the [release page](https://github.com/gloom-sh/gloomberb/releases/latest).

items: **Terminal:** the installer adds `gloomberb` to your PATH, so open a new terminal window. PowerShell works.
**Charts:** Windows Terminal has no Kitty graphics, so terminal charts draw as text. The desktop app draws them in full.
**Data:** `%USERPROFILE%\.gloomberb`, printed by `gloomberb version`. `GLOOMBERB_HOME` moves it.
**Git and Bun:** Bun ships with the app. Git is needed only to install plugins.
**Versions:** Windows 11 x64. Windows 10 and ARM PCs (x64 emulation) are untested.

blocks.text: Terminal only, with [Bun](https://bun.sh), in PowerShell:

blocks.code: bun install -g gloomberb

blocks.text: Browser
[Open term.gloom.sh](https://term.gloom.sh) without an account: search, delayed quotes, charts, delayed news and most panes work in a one-pane workspace. Layouts stay in your browser.

A free sign-in unlocks account-backed panes such as filings, analysts, supply chain and scanners, plus sync and sharing. Some research panes and real-time data require Pro. Browser builds cannot connect brokers or install local plugins.
Check it works

blocks.code:
gloomberb
gloomberb version
gloomberb doctor

blocks.text: `gloomberb` opens the terminal UI. `version` prints the data folder, and `doctor` checks that config, the cache database, plugins, and capabilities load.
Update

rows: Updates itself; `u` retries a failed update.
Updates itself; `Check for Updates` in the menu or command bar checks now.

blocks.text: Release channels

The app updates from **stable** releases, the ones on the [changelog](/changelog). **Nightly** is a daily build of main that gets fixes first and can break. To switch, run **Release Channel** from the command bar (on the Mac, also **Gloomberb > Release Channel...**), or in a terminal:

blocks.code: gloomberb config set updates.channel nightly

blocks.text: Switching back to stable never installs an older version: your nightly build stays until a newer stable release is out. Nightly applies to the desktop app and the terminal app; Homebrew, Bun and the install script always get stable.
Next: [your first session](/docs/first-session).

pages.title: Portfolios and rebalancing
pages.lead: Give each holding a target weight. PF then shows how far each one has drifted and the trade that brings it back.

blocks.text: Build a portfolio
A portfolio is what you hold: shares, what you paid for them, and cash. It stays on your device. In the app, run **New Portfolio**; in a shell:

blocks.code:
gloomberb portfolio create Core
gloomberb portfolio position set Core VTI 40 280
gloomberb portfolio position set Core BND 60 72
gloomberb portfolio cash set Core 2000 USD

blocks.text: Set targets
A target is the weight you want a holding to have, as a share of the whole portfolio. Cash can have one too.

blocks.code:
gloomberb portfolio target set Core VTI 60
gloomberb portfolio target set Core BND 35
gloomberb portfolio target set Core CASH 5

blocks.text: Read the drift table
`PF` and `gloomberb portfolio show Core` add four columns once targets are set:

rows: Share of the total value, cash included
Weight minus target, in percentage points (pp)
Shares to buy (+) or sell (-) to get back to target

blocks.text: Rebalance
VTI is 11.1pp over its target, so the table says sell 6 shares. BND is 15.4pp under, so buy 47. Make both trades and every drift lands near 0pp.
`gloomberb portfolio show Core --explain` prints these terms under the table. `gloomberb catalog glossary` lists every term the terminal uses.

items: Targets need not add up to 100%; the report says what is unallocated.
Trades use the current price and leave out fees, taxes and lot sizes.
A broker portfolio uses the cash its account reports.
In the PF pane the columns read `WEIGHT`, `TGT WT`, `DRIFT` and `TRADE`.

blocks.text: Related: [PF](/docs/functions#pf), [CLI](/docs/cli-functions#portfolios-and-notes).

pages.lead: Fix launch, command, data, chart, layout, account, and broker problems by symptom.

blocks.text: Quick check

rows: Check the pane entitlement and lightning toggle.

blocks.text: Will not launch

items: `Bad CPU type in executable` on macOS: an Intel Mac running the Apple Silicon app. Delete `/Applications/Gloomberb.app` and rerun `curl -fsSL gloom.sh/install | bash` for the Intel terminal build.
`gloomberb doctor` shows runtime errors.
Update with the same method you installed with. See [Install and update](/docs/getting-started).

blocks.text: Command missing

items: Commands: `Cmd/Ctrl+K` or `Ctrl+P`. Backtick is tickers only.
Search the command name if you forgot the prefix, or `HELP` in the app and `gloomberb help` in a shell.
Plugin command: `gloomberb plugin list`. Plugin missing: `gloomberb plugin doctor <name-or-path>`, see [Plugins](/docs/plugins).
Some commands need a ticker: `GP AAPL`, not `GP`.
Not sure what a pane shows? `F1` opens its help card.

blocks.text: Wrong company in ticker search
The same symbol exists on several exchanges. Check name, type, and exchange before `Enter`. Search the full company name when a symbol is ambiguous.

items: Wait for loading to finish, then `r`.
Read the status: delayed, stale, error, or auth.
`gloomberb provider status` lists enabled providers.
Check the pane supports the instrument. SEC filings cover supported US securities only.
Hosted panes may need login, verification, or an entitlement.

Delayed is normal on Free; Pro is live where the pane supports it. Check the [lightning toggle](/docs/cloud-and-data#live-toggle) is on.
Chart or terminal graphics

items: Use Ghostty, Kitty, or WezTerm.
Enlarge the window, refresh the pane.
`0` in a focused chart resets the viewport.
`CR` cycles the chart renderer: Auto, Kitty, Braille.

items: `Tab` / `Shift+Tab`: it may be open but unfocused.
`LAY` or `Cmd/Ctrl+1` through `9` to switch to the right layout.
`GL` to tile what is visible.
`Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+W` closes floating panes covering the workspace.

blocks.text: Deleting a layout does not delete portfolios, watchlists, or notes.
Login, sync, or chat

items: Search `Log In`; confirm the account is verified.
`ACM` shows profile and plan.

blocks.text: Broker data or trading

items: `BR` checks the connection before `IBKR`.
Cloud login and broker authorization are separate.
Market data, account sync, and order authorization can fail independently.
Review the account and the order preview before submitting. Never test with a real order.

blocks.text: Report a problem

Send Feedback from the status bar, `FB`, or Help. It attaches the app version, scrubbed logs, and an optional screenshot, and works signed out. Or open an issue in the [tracker](https://github.com/gloom-sh/gloomberb/issues).

pages.lead: OPX shows where open interest sits on a US option underlying; GEX estimates the gamma dealers carry against it

blocks.text: `[` and `]` step through expiries. On GEX, `All` sums every expiry.
How GEX is estimated
Nobody publishes who holds which option. GEX assumes customers sell calls and buy puts, so **dealers are long every call and short every put**. Net GEX is call gamma minus put gamma.
Positive means dealers hedge against a move: they sell rallies and buy dips. Negative means they hedge with it.

rows: Dollars of dealer delta per 1% move in the underlying
The spot level, within 15% of spot, where net GEX changes sign
The strike with the most call gamma, in one expiry or all
The strike with the most put gamma, in one expiry or all
Net GEX if dealers held only 25% to 75% of each side

blocks.text: The Expiries tab's net GEX uses the same strikes and volatilities as `All`, so its rows add up to it.

items: Gamma per contract is Black-Scholes gamma with the forward at spot, times the 100-share multiplier. Time runs to 16:00 New York on the expiry date, at least one hour.
Each strike's volatility comes from its expiry's out-of-the-money quotes, linear between quoted strikes and flat beyond. An expiry without usable quotes is left out and named.
GEX at a strike is gamma × 100 × spot × 1% of spot × open interest.
The flip reprices net GEX from 15% below to 15% above spot in 0.25% steps, each strike keeping its volatility, and takes the sign change nearest spot.
A tie for a wall goes to the lowest strike. Walls mark where hedging is heaviest, not levels the price has to respect.
The range sets the dealer share anywhere from 25% to 75% of the calls and, separately, of the puts. The low end is 25% of call gamma minus 75% of put gamma, the high end the reverse.
The headline figure counts all of the open interest, so it can sit outside the range. When the range spans zero, the sign of net GEX depends on who holds which side.

On SPX and XSP, matched call and put open interest at paired round strikes far from spot is read as box spreads and taken out of both sides. Net GEX and the flip stay the same; the range narrows and says `boxes out`.

blocks.text: During a session, GEX applies today's spot and volatilities to open interest from about two sessions back.

Keep in mind

items: GEX is a model on open interest, not measured dealer positions. On single stocks the customer side can be the reverse.

pages.lead: Use the semantic remote API to inspect and control a running Gloomberb desktop or TUI session.

blocks.text: What this is
The remote API drives a running Gloomberb app. Agents and scripts read semantic state, open panes, navigate tickers, arrange layouts, and call plugin capabilities, with no screen coordinates.

Use it to operate the live desktop or TUI, and to capture a pane of the desktop app as it looks right now (`pane.screenshot`). Use the [CLI](/docs/cli-functions) for headless data, reports, and screenshots of a function with no app open.

This remote API: no account, no network, nothing asks
Claude Code, Codex or another assistant connected to Gloom Cloud

The [MCP server](/docs/mcp) with [Terminal control](/docs/mcp#terminal-control): the same operations, one MCP for data and the terminal, and the app asks you before an assistant takes over and before anything leaves the app
Anything that needs Cloud data with no terminal open

Terminal control

Terminal control reaches everything the [remote API](/docs/agents) does in your open, signed-in desktop or TUI: read the screen, open and arrange panes, navigate tickers, switch and edit layouts, semantic UI actions and plugin capabilities. The app asks once before an assistant takes over; plugin capabilities, button presses, commands and anything that reaches an outside service (orders, transfers, messages) ask you in the app on every call, and an unanswered one is denied after 60 seconds.

blocks.text: Each tool takes `device?` (an id or name from `terminal.devices`). Descriptions carry the operation's tier and whether you confirm each call. A call that waits on you longer than 45 seconds answers `pending` with a `callId`; read the outcome with `terminal.call_result`. With no app open, tools answer `no_terminal`. Revoke an assistant in the app (Account Management, Agents), or revoke its key or disconnect it here, and its next call stops.
Results and limits

Each call returns text plus `structuredContent` with `status` (`ok`, `partial` when a limit removed rows, or `error`), `rowCount`, `truncated`, `asOf` and `data`. Results are capped at 256 KB. A failed source returns `status: "error"` with `data.error = { code, source, reason }`. `terminal.pane.screenshot` returns the same JSON as text plus an image block, and no `structuredContent`, since some clients read only that and would drop the image.
Creating keys needs Pro. Any valid key can `initialize` and `tools/list`; tool calls need Pro, except `portfolio.*`, and get real-time quotes and the live news wire.

Keys allow 120 requests a minute and 5,000 a day; over the limit returns `429` with `Retry-After`. If Pro lapses, keys stay but tool calls are refused. Revoking a key applies on the next request; a disconnected client's token expires within two hours, and its terminal calls stop at once.

pages.title: Google Sheets
pages.lead: =GLOOM and =GLOOMH in Google Sheets: live prices, fundamentals and history with Bloomberg tickers and field names.

blocks.text: Setup

rows: Create a key with **Market data only** access in [Cloud settings, Agents](/cloud/account?view=agents). It needs [Gloom Pro](/cloud). A broader key is refused, since every editor of the sheet can read it.
In your sheet, open **Extensions > Apps Script**.
Replace everything in `Code.gs` with [gloom.sh/sheets/gloom.js](https://gloom.sh/sheets/gloom.js) and save.

Reload the sheet, then **Gloom > Set API key** and paste the key. It is tried once and not saved if it is broader than Market data only, revoked or on the free plan. The first time, Google asks you to authorize your own script and may say it is unverified: choose **Advanced**, then **Go to** your project. If the key prompt does not open after that, choose **Set API key** again.
Type `=GLOOM("AAPL US Equity", "PX_LAST")` in any cell.

blocks.text: Sample

A Bloomberg workbook ports with find and replace: `BDP(` to `GLOOM(`, `BDH(` to `GLOOMH(`. Bloomberg tickers answer as Bloomberg does, down to London prices in pence (`CRNCY` is `GBp`), so the workbook's own arithmetic still holds.
Coming from Bloomberg? [BDP and BDH next to their Sheets formulas](/answers/bloomberg-bdp-bdh-google-sheets).
Or fill the whole table from one cell: `=GLOOM(A2:A4, B1:D1)`. Blank or repeated tickers and fields keep their row or column, so the table stays lined up with its labels.
History, dates down the first column: `=GLOOMH("CL1 Comdty", "PX_LAST", "2026-01-01", TODAY(), "weekly")`.

Dates can be sheet dates or text as `2026-01-01` or `20260101`; an empty end is today. The period is `daily` (default), `weekly`, `monthly`, `quarterly` or `annual`. Bloomberg's `Per=W`, `Per=M`, `Per=CW` and `Per=CM` work too.
How it behaves

items: Tickers and fields are the [REST API's](/docs/rest-api): Gloom, exchange-suffixed or Bloomberg forms, Gloom field ids or Bloomberg mnemonics. `=GLOOM(ticker, field, "quarterly")` reads the latest quarter for statement fields.
A value that does not exist comes back as `#N/A` text with the reason, like Bloomberg's, so `IFERROR` does not hide it. Use `ISNUMBER`.

The first cell that needs data fetches every `GLOOM` formula in the sheet together, so hundreds of cells cost a few requests (a unit per 20 tickers for prices, per 5 for fundamentals and estimates). Prices refresh after a minute, other values after an hour, and each `GLOOMH` table after five minutes (six hours when its range ended in the past). **Gloom > Refresh data** fetches again.

A revoked key, a free plan or a rate limit shows in the cells and pauses fetching for a few minutes. Fix the cause, then **Gloom > Refresh data**; **Gloom > Test connection** checks the key. A value not ready in time reads `#N/A Not ready...` and is asked for again on the next recalculation.

The key sits in the script's properties, which every editor of the sheet can read. That is why only Market data only keys work here; revoke the key in Cloud settings if the sheet is shared too widely.

pages.title: Plugins
pages.lead: Install, build, and publish Gloomberb plugins: panes, commands, CLI commands, data capabilities, and UI.

blocks.text: How plugins fit

A plugin can register panes, pane templates, settings and quick controls, command-bar commands, CLI commands, data capabilities, ticker actions, context menus, shortcuts, brokers, and renderer-neutral UI.
Import only from the `gloomberb/*` exports, never OpenTUI, Electrobun, DOM, or private Gloomberb source paths. Full API: [PLUGINS.md](https://github.com/gloom-sh/gloomberb/blob/main/PLUGINS.md).
Install and manage

blocks.code:
gloomberb install user/repo
gloomberb install https://github.com/user/repo
gloomberb plugins
gloomberb update
gloomberb update my-plugin
gloomberb remove my-plugin
gloomberb plugin enable my-plugin
gloomberb plugin disable my-plugin

blocks.text: Plugins live in `~/.gloomberb/plugins/`. Installs from `PL` load at once; restart after a CLI install or an edit.
Type the code of an official plugin you do not have, such as `POLL` or `TV`, and the command bar offers to install it, then opens it. The web terminal lists where to get it instead.
Not loading? `gloomberb plugin doctor <name-or-path>` checks the entry, export, id, targets, hosts, and browser build, even for a plugin that failed to load.

blocks.caption: PL toggles first-party and installed plugins from the command bar.

blocks.text: Make a minimal plugin
Create `hello-gloom/index.ts`. It registers one in-app command and one shell command, no dependencies:
Link the checkout, check it, and run the shell command:

blocks.code:
gloomberb plugin link ./hello-gloom
gloomberb plugin doctor hello-gloom
gloomberb hello Vince --json

blocks.text: Restart Gloomberb, then type `HELLO` in the command bar. For an interactive pane, copy [gloom-hackernews](https://github.com/gloom-sh/gloom-hackernews).
Publish to the directory
[gloom.sh/plugins](/plugins) lists every public repo tagged `gloom-plugin`. Add the topic, then describe the plugin in `gloom.json` at the root:
The older names still work: the `gloomberb-plugin` topic, `gloomberb.json`, and `minGloomberb`. Where both exist, `gloom` wins.

rows: Required. Repos without one are skipped.
Where the plugin runs. A plugin that opens a local socket should not claim `web`.

What it adds, shown as "What it adds" on its page and in the marketplace: `panes` (pane ids), `capabilities` (ids such as `asset-data.gloomberb-cloud`), `broker: true`. Built-ins report this from the running app; installable plugins must declare it, or the page says the plugin adds nothing. `shortcuts` lists the command-bar codes it answers to (`code`, `name`, a one-line `description`): the app offers to install an official plugin when one is typed, and never offers other plugins that way.
A square `.svg`, `.png`, or `.webp` in the repo, read from the default branch. URLs are rejected. Without one, a glyph is drawn from the categories.

blocks.text: Nothing is reviewed: the directory is a listing, not a gate. Once a listed repo has a tag, `install` and `update` land on a tag, not the default branch, so tag each release.

pages.title: News API
pages.lead: Use Gloomberb's standalone market-news API in your own financial product.

blocks.text: Separate product
The News API is Gloomberb's market news for your own product, backend, model pipeline, or dashboard. It is not needed to use the app and is billed separately from [Gloom Cloud](/docs/cloud-and-data).
The [financial news API](/news) page shows the live wire and has the Get API key button.
See also: [Gloom Datasets](/docs/datasets), a separate paid API for alternative signals, filings, macro, news and market data, with its own `gds_` keys.
Access levels

rows: Delayed 12 hours. Real-time with a paid [Gloom Datasets](/docs/datasets) plan.

blocks.text: Both get the same v1 response, including ticker links and source clusters, and neither is metered. Create or rotate a key from [News API account](/news/account).
Authentication
Every `/v1/news` request requires a News API key or a [Gloom Datasets](/docs/datasets) key (`gds_`). Use either header style:

blocks.code:
Authorization: Bearer gloom_news_...

x-api-key: gloom_news_...

blocks.text: Check access state with:

blocks.code:
curl -s 'https://api.gloom.sh/v1/me' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer gloom_news_...'

blocks.text: `/v1/me` returns the plan, whether the key has full access, billing interval/status, and `dataDelaySeconds`.
The market data endpoints under `/v1` (quotes, data, history) take Gloom keys instead; see the [REST API](/docs/rest-api).
List news

blocks.code:
curl -s 'https://api.gloom.sh/v1/news?feed=top&limit=25' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer gloom_news_...'

rows: Defaults to the service default when omitted. `ticker` is newest first by last published time.
Comma-separated. Required for `feed=ticker`. Use exchange-qualified symbols for ambiguous tickers.

blocks.text: More filters:
Feed examples

blocks.code:
curl -s 'https://api.gloom.sh/v1/news?feed=ticker&tickers=NVDA:XNAS&tickerTier=primary' \
  -H 'x-api-key: gloom_news_...'

blocks.text: Story detail

blocks.code:
curl -s 'https://api.gloom.sh/v1/news/{storyId}' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer gloom_news_...'

blocks.text: Detail returns the story plus its source items. Top and breaking lists include source items inline.
Metadata

blocks.code:
curl -s 'https://api.gloom.sh/v1/news/sources' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer gloom_news_...'

curl -s 'https://api.gloom.sh/v1/news/facets' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer gloom_news_...'

blocks.text: Use these to populate filters in your app.
Response shape
Abridged; each story also carries `topics`, `sectors`, `scope`, first and last seen times, `flags`, `breaking` detail, `variantCount` and `sourceCount`.
Ticker errors
Ticker problems return `400` with a `reasonCode`:

rows: Send an exchange-qualified symbol from `candidates`, such as `AAPL:XNAS`, or a local suffix where supported.

pages.title: Gloom Datasets
pages.lead: GPU prices, supply chains, hiring and attention signals alongside filings, macro, news and market data. One paid REST API. Every value cited.

blocks.text: What it is

Gloom Datasets serves the data Gloom stores to your own systems over REST. It is a separate product with its own site at [datasets.gloom.sh](https://datasets.gloom.sh) and its own keys and plans, billed separately from [Gloom Cloud](/docs/cloud-and-data). The app does not need it.

Every dataset call returns `data` and `meta`. `meta` names the dataset and its sources, with attribution and usage terms, plus `asOf`, `historyStarts`, `coverage` and `lastUpdated`. A value the stored data cannot establish is `null`.
Datasets

items: **Alternative data:** GPU rental prices, supply chain, hiring postings and momentum, social mentions, app attention, power and grid, perpetuals, catalysts and litigation, research attention, congressional trades, operating exposure.

**Filings and company text:** KPIs and guidance, executive pay, risk factors, 8-K events, transcripts, credit documents, debt maturities, revenue breakdown, SEC filings, insiders and 13F, document search.
**News:** Real-time stories, sources and topics.
**Macro and positioning:** CPI, EIA inventories, COT, yield curves and macro series, central bank rates, short volume and interest, CDS, government awards.

**Market data and fundamentals:** Quotes and history, financial statements, statistics, profiles, earnings, estimates, IPOs, M&A, screener, options and gamma positioning, futures, rate path, crypto, session tape.

blocks.text: See the [full dataset reference](https://datasets.gloom.sh/docs) for routes, parameters, examples and credits.

The base URL is `https://api.gloom.sh/v1`. `/v1/datasets` lists served datasets, `/v1/datasets/cost` prices a call, and `/v1/datasets/{dataset}/sample` returns a static example. The reference labels illustrative values or trimmed real output. None needs a key.
Keys
Gloom Datasets keys start with `gds_`. They come with a plan and are created in the [console](https://datasets.gloom.sh/console). Send one as `Authorization: Bearer gds_...` or `x-api-key`.

They are different keys from the Gloom API's. A Gloom Pro key (`gloom_mcp_`) or a News API key (`gloom_news_`) gets `401 wrong_key` on a dataset route, and a `gds_` key gets `401` on the Gloom API's own routes, such as the [REST API](/docs/rest-api), but reads the [News API](/docs/news-api) at no credit cost.
Plans
Paid plans only: an account without a plan has no key.
Enterprise is an annual contract. Basic and Desk are also sold yearly at ten months' price.
Each call spends credits from the plan; the `X-Credits-Cost` and `X-Credits-Remaining` headers say what it cost and what is left.

Credits, rate limits, usage rights and the founding offer (40% off Basic and Desk for 12 months, for the first 100 paid accounts until December 4, 2026) are on [Pricing](https://datasets.gloom.sh/pricing).
Docs

items: [Quickstart](https://datasets.gloom.sh/docs/quickstart): a plan, a key, one call, then the same call from Python and TypeScript.
[API reference](https://datasets.gloom.sh/docs): datasets, routes, credits, errors and the OpenAPI document.
[Console](https://datasets.gloom.sh/console): account, billing, keys and usage.

lessons.title: What a stock is
lessons.summary: A share is a small slice of a company, so owning one means owning a tiny piece of everything the company has and earns.

lessons.title: Funds, ETFs and indices
lessons.summary: A fund is a basket you can own, an index is a ruler that measures a basket, and an ETF is a fund that trades like a stock.

lessons.title: Exchanges, hours and tickers
lessons.summary: An exchange is the marketplace where shares change hands during set hours, and every listed security has a short code called a ticker.

lessons.title: Reading a quote
lessons.summary: A quote is not one price but five numbers (last trade, best bid, best ask, the spread between them, and volume) that together tell you what you would really pay to trade now.

lessons.title: Orders, long, short and margin
lessons.summary: An order is your instruction to a broker, and long, short and margin say which way you bet and whether you borrowed to do it.

lessons.title: Returns and percentages
lessons.summary: A return is the gain or loss compared with what you paid, written as a percentage so that a 20 dollar stock and a 2,000 dollar stock can be compared.

lessons.title: Understanding risk
lessons.summary: Four numbers describe how much an investment can hurt: volatility (how bumpy), drawdown (how deep the worst fall), correlation (do two things move together) and beta (how much it moves with the market).

lessons.title: Who is who on Wall Street
lessons.summary: Wall Street is a few kinds of players: the buy side invests money, the sell side sells it services and trades, the plumbing (market makers, prime brokers, clearing) makes trades happen and settle, and regulators watch them all.

lessons.title: How information reaches prices
lessons.summary: Prices move when new information (results, filings, economic numbers, central bank decisions, news) differs from what people already expected: only the surprise moves the price.

lessons.title: The macro machine
lessons.summary: "Macro" is the economy as a whole (output, inflation and jobs) plus the interest rate the central bank sets to steer them, and it is why one number can move every market at once.

lessons.title: Derivatives in one page
lessons.summary: A derivative is a contract whose value comes from something else (a stock, an index, oil, an interest rate), and the three big families are futures, options and swaps.

lessons.title: Bonds in one page
lessons.summary: A bond is a loan you can buy and sell, paying fixed interest until a set repayment date, and its price and its yield always move in opposite directions.

lessons.title: The cheat sheet
lessons.summary: The whole chapter on one page, to re-read before a meeting: a 100-word summary, the numbers to remember and who is who.

lessons.title: Your first 10 minutes
lessons.summary: Gloom is a grid of screens you open by typing a short code and a ticker; in ten minutes you can set up your holdings, open a company, see what moves today, set an alert and find help.

lessons.title: The command bar and function codes
lessons.summary: The command bar is the one place you type everything: a function code, then what it applies to (DES AAPL), or plain words to search; it answers "how do I open X?".

lessons.title: Tickers, listings and asset classes
lessons.summary: The same company can trade under several tickers on several exchanges, so Gloom lets you pick the exact listing with a suffix or a search and filter by asset class.

lessons.title: Panes, focus and linking (WIN, GL, PS, LMA)
lessons.summary: Every function opens in a pane, one pane at a time has the focus and receives your keys, and panes can be moved, tidied and linked so they follow a list.

lessons.title: Layouts and desks (LAY, DESK)
lessons.summary: A layout is a saved screen of panes, DESK adds a ready-made one for a kind of market, and LAY switches, adds and shares layouts.

lessons.title: Getting help (HELP, F1, CHG, FB)
lessons.summary: HELP opens the guide and every function, and F1 opens the help card of the pane in front of you, including how fresh its data is on your plan.

lessons.title: Free, Pro and how fresh your data is (UPGRADE, CONN)
lessons.summary: Every number has an age (real-time, 15 minutes behind, daily or on release), and the help card's Data line and the clock mark on a quote tell you which.

lessons.title: Gloom from your shell (the CLI)
lessons.summary: The functions you open in panes also run from your computer's command line, printing a table or JSON and CSV for scripts and spreadsheets.

lessons.title: Make it yours (VIEW, PL, TH, LANG, FONT, SB, VF, CR)
lessons.summary: VIEW builds your own table from any data function, PL manages plugins, and a few short commands change the theme, language, font size and visual effects.

lessons.title: Portfolios and watchlists (PF, AP, AW, RP, RW)
lessons.summary: PF shows what you own (positions, cost, profit and loss) and what you follow (watchlists) with live prices, and AP, AW, RP and RW add or remove tickers from anywhere.

lessons.title: Portfolio risk (PORT, MARS)
lessons.summary: PORT (also MARS) measures your portfolio's risk against a benchmark: how much it swings, its worst fall, a bad-day loss estimate, and what a crash or a rate jump would do to it.

lessons.title: How big a position? (KELLY)
lessons.summary: KELLY turns your own guesses (chance of being right, upside, downside) into a position size, caps it with your risk limits, and says how much to add or trim.

lessons.title: Alerts (ALRT, SA)
lessons.summary: An alert watches the market for you, firing on a price level or an event such as an earnings date, a filing or an insider trade, and ALRT lists them all.

lessons.title: Notes and theses (NOTE, THESIS)
lessons.summary: Notes are your free-form memory (NOTE), and a thesis (THESIS) is a checkable reason for holding something, with pillars that must stay true and kill conditions that would make you sell.

lessons.title: Chat and teams (CHAT, DM, TEAM)
lessons.summary: CHAT opens public channels by topic, DM @user starts a private conversation, and TEAM creates a private group that shares layouts, lists, notes and its own chat.

lessons.title: Your account and your broker (ACM, BR, IBKR)
lessons.summary: ACM manages your Gloom account, and BR connects a brokerage account so your real positions appear in a portfolio and stay in sync.

lessons.title: The AI helpers (ASKG, AI, AGENT)
lessons.summary: Gloom has three AI helpers: Ask Gloom (ASKG) answers with Gloom's own tools and cites its sources, the AI screener (AI) turns a sentence into a list of tickers, and the agent (AGENT) can operate the app for you.

lessons.title: The overview page (DES)
lessons.summary: DES is the front page of a ticker: quote, day and 52-week ranges, the long chart, returns, key numbers, and tabs into everything else, on one screen.

lessons.title: A board of quotes (QQ)
lessons.summary: QQ is a wall of tiles, one per ticker, each with the last price, today's change, a one-month sparkline and the month's low and high.

lessons.title: A fund's official documents (ETF)
lessons.summary: ETF lists a US fund's filings with the SEC (prospectus, holdings reports, shareholder reports) and opens any of them.

lessons.title: Earnings ripple (RIPL)
lessons.summary: RIPL lists the big customers and suppliers of your holdings that report earnings in the next 30 days, with how much revenue links them.

lessons.title: Reading a price chart (GP)
lessons.summary: GP is the price chart: candles on top, volume below, a multi-year range by default.

lessons.title: The intraday chart (GIP)
lessons.summary: GIP charts one trading session (or the last five) minute by minute, with volume below and the session's start and end marked.

lessons.title: Moving averages, RSI and MACD (chart indicators)
lessons.summary: Indicators are formulas on past prices drawn on the chart: moving averages smooth the noise, RSI measures how one-sided recent moves were, and MACD compares a fast average with a slow one.

lessons.title: VWAP, bands, ATR and price levels (chart tools)
lessons.summary: VWAP, Bollinger Bands, ATR, volume profile and your own price levels are different ways of asking whether today's price is normal, and a level can become an alert.

lessons.title: Chart anything together (G)
lessons.summary: G puts any series (a price, a statement line, a multiple, an economic series or a formula) on one timeline so you can see whether they move together.

lessons.title: The price history table (HP)
lessons.summary: HP is the chart turned into rows: one line per bar with open, high, low, close, the change from the bar before, and volume.

lessons.title: The returns table (RETURN)
lessons.summary: RETURN lists the return of each period and the return since the start of the window, so you can see how small moves compound.

lessons.title: Seasonality (SEAS)
lessons.summary: SEAS lays out a ticker's monthly returns year by year with each month's average, median and share of up years, and shows why calendar patterns are weak evidence.

lessons.title: Backtesting a rule (BT, BTST)
lessons.summary: BT (also BTST) replays a simple buy-and-sell rule on a stock's daily history and compares it with buying and holding, trade by trade.

lessons.title: The trade tape (TAS)
lessons.summary: TAS (time and sales) lists every reported trade in a US stock as it prints, with time, price, shares, venue and conditions, and the VWAP of the trades seen.

lessons.title: The best bid and ask over time (QR)
lessons.summary: QR (quote recap) shows every change in the best bid and ask across US exchanges, with sizes, venues and the spread in basis points.

lessons.title: The three financial statements (FA)
lessons.summary: Every company reports three tables (the income statement, the balance sheet and the cash flow statement), and FA shows all three by year or quarter.

lessons.title: Ratios that matter (FA ratio tabs)
lessons.summary: A ratio divides one number by another so companies of any size can be compared: margins and returns for quality, debt ratios for risk, and valuation multiples for price.

lessons.title: Red and green flags (DIAG)
lessons.summary: DIAG turns a company's filings and numbers into a short verdict and lists of red flags, green flags and items to watch, each with the fact, a reading and its source filing.

lessons.title: Revenue by segment and company KPIs (SEG, KPIS)
lessons.summary: SEG splits a company's revenue by product, segment and region from its filings, and KPIS tracks the operating numbers it reports beyond the statements, each with its source quote.

lessons.title: What growth is priced in? (RDCF)
lessons.summary: RDCF runs a discounted cash flow model backwards, finding the yearly growth today's value assumes and setting it next to the growth the company actually delivered.

lessons.title: The earnings calendar and implied moves (ERN, EVTS)
lessons.summary: EVTS lists who reports this week with the move options are pricing and the move the stock usually makes, and ERN <ticker> shows one company's next report and its history.

lessons.title: Estimates, surprises and revisions (EE, EM)
lessons.summary: EE sets analysts' consensus estimates next to the results actually reported, and EM tracks how that consensus is being revised.

lessons.title: Guidance (GUID, GUIDE)
lessons.summary: Guidance is the company's own forecast, and GUID and GUIDE set it next to the consensus and track each guided number, its raises and cuts, and the actual result.

lessons.title: Earnings calls (CALLS)
lessons.summary: CALLS lists a company's earnings calls and opens each transcript with speakers, the analyst Q&A, a tone score, and the guidance and quotes pulled out of it.

lessons.title: Analyst ratings and price targets (ANR)
lessons.summary: ANR shows sell-side ratings and 12-month price targets: the average target and its history, the upside to it, and every recent action by firm.

lessons.title: Dividends and corporate actions (DVD, EVT)
lessons.summary: DVD shows a stock's dividend history, yield, payout ratio and growth, and EVT puts dividends, splits, earnings dates and estimates on one timeline.

lessons.title: Catalysts (CATL)
lessons.summary: CATL is a calendar of dated events that can move a stock (trial results, regulators' decisions, court deadlines, tariffs), each with its date basis, status and source.

lessons.title: Mergers and acquisitions (MA)
lessons.summary: MA lists pending, rumored and closed takeover deals with their terms, their stage and, for listed targets, the arbitrage spread between the offer and the market price.

lessons.title: Comparing returns (CMP)
lessons.summary: CMP draws two or more tickers as percentage returns from the same start date, so you can see which did better over the same window.
lessons.chapter: Compare, screen and follow the money

lessons.title: Relative valuation (RV)
lessons.summary: RV puts a peer group in one table at today's prices (size, P/E, forward P/E, EV/sales, free cash flow yield and growth) so you can judge a company's price against its peers.
lessons.chapter: Compare, screen and follow the money

lessons.title: Valuation over time (GE, GF, PEB)
lessons.summary: PEB, GE and GF turn valuation snapshots into history: a stock's price against fixed P/E lines, multiples over time for several tickers, and statement lines across companies.
lessons.chapter: Compare, screen and follow the money

lessons.title: How stocks move together (GR, CORR)
lessons.summary: GR studies how two tickers move together (ratio, rolling correlation, regression) and CORR builds a correlation matrix for a whole basket.
lessons.chapter: Compare, screen and follow the money

lessons.title: Screening the market (EQS)
lessons.summary: EQS keeps only the stocks in its stored universe that meet all your rules (valuation, growth, margins, liquidity, ownership and more) and ranks the matches.
lessons.chapter: Compare, screen and follow the money

lessons.title: Big holders and 13F filings (HDS, 13F)
lessons.summary: HDS shows a stock's biggest institutional holders from quarterly 13F filings, and 13F browses the funds themselves: holdings, changes, crowded positions and estimated performance.
lessons.chapter: Compare, screen and follow the money

lessons.title: Insider trades (INS)
lessons.summary: INS lists the trades company insiders must report on Form 4 within two business days (buys, sells, awards, gifts and tax payments) with name, size and price.
lessons.chapter: Compare, screen and follow the money

lessons.title: Congress trades (CG)
lessons.summary: CG lists the trades members of Congress must disclose within 45 days, with the member, the asset, buy or sell, the amount band, the owner and how late it was reported.
lessons.chapter: Compare, screen and follow the money

lessons.title: Short interest and squeezes (SI, SIV, SIW)
lessons.summary: SI shows short interest over time with days to cover, SIV the daily short share of off-exchange volume (a noisier number), and SIW ranks your names by how crowded the short is.
lessons.chapter: Compare, screen and follow the money

lessons.title: SEC filings and 8-K events (SEC, EK)
lessons.summary: SEC lists a company's filings on the SEC's public EDGAR database and opens them, and EK reads its 8-K event notices item by item with a short summary of each.
lessons.chapter: Compare, screen and follow the money

lessons.title: Risk factors (RISK)
lessons.summary: RISK groups the risk factors in a company's 10-K by theme and shows what was added, dropped or reworded since the previous year.
lessons.chapter: Compare, screen and follow the money

lessons.title: Executive pay (EXEC)
lessons.summary: EXEC reads the yearly proxy statement into key pay figures (CEO total pay, the pay ratio, the share in stock, shareholder support) and a table of the top executives.
lessons.chapter: Compare, screen and follow the money

lessons.title: Attention: research and social buzz (ATTN, BUZZ)
lessons.summary: ATTN ranks the tickers Gloom users are researching against each ticker's usual level, and BUZZ counts the day's posts on X naming a ticker, with the top posts and their stance.
