lessons.title: What an option is (calls and puts)
lessons.summary: An option is the right, but not the duty, to buy or sell something at a fixed price before a deadline, and you pay a fee for that right.

lessons.title: Value and payoff at expiry
lessons.summary: An option's price is what it is worth if used right now (intrinsic value) plus a bet on the future (time value), and at expiry only the first part is left.

lessons.title: The Greeks in plain words (OVME)
lessons.summary: The Greeks say how an option's price reacts when the stock moves (delta, gamma), when time passes (theta) or when expected swings change (vega), and OVME computes them for any option you describe.

lessons.title: Implied vs realized volatility
lessons.summary: Realized volatility is how much a stock actually moved and implied volatility is how much option prices assume it will move, and comparing the two is the core question of a volatility desk.

lessons.title: What a volatility desk does
lessons.summary: A bank's volatility desk makes markets in options, hedges away direction every day, and keeps a book of exposures to movement (gamma) and to volatility (vega), earning the spread and, on average, implied above realized volatility.

lessons.title: The options chain (OMON)
lessons.summary: OMON is the menu of every option on one stock: one tab per expiry, one row per strike, calls left and puts right with quotes and Greeks, and a strip of volatility numbers on top.

lessons.title: Building a position (OSA)
lessons.summary: OSA turns several option legs into one position and shows its value at any stock price, date and volatility, with breakevens, maximum profit and loss, and the combined Greeks.

lessons.title: The volatility surface and skew (OVDV)
lessons.summary: Implied volatility changes with the strike (the skew) and with the expiry (the term structure), and OVDV fits the whole surface from option quotes.

lessons.title: Realized volatility and the cone (HVG, HVT)
lessons.summary: HVG charts realized volatility over windows from 10 to 260 sessions, and HVT (the cone) places each window's current value in its own range over the past year or two.

lessons.title: Is implied vol high or low? (HIVG, VCA)
lessons.summary: HIVG charts a stock's implied volatility history with IV rank and percentile, and VCA ranks a list of tickers as rich, fair or cheap on those and a few other clues.

lessons.title: The VIX and volatility indices (VIX, VOLS)
lessons.summary: The VIX is the 30-day implied volatility of the S&P 500, and VIX and VOLS show its curve across horizons and its cousins in bonds, oil, gold and single stocks.

lessons.title: Open interest and max pain (OPX)
lessons.summary: OPX shows open interest (contracts still open) by strike and expiry, with the put/call ratio and max pain, the expiry price at which option holders would collect least.

lessons.title: Dealer gamma (GEX)
lessons.summary: Dealer gamma (GEX) estimates how much option dealers would trade per 1% move to stay hedged, under an assumption about who holds which option, and where that estimate flips sign.

lessons.title: Options flow (FLOW)
lessons.summary: FLOW is a live tape of large option trades on the busiest US contracts (sweeps, blocks and big-premium prints) with ticker, contract, size, premium and implied volatility.

lessons.title: Futures from zero (FUT)
lessons.summary: A futures contract is a standard, exchange-traded promise to buy or sell a set quantity on a set month at a price agreed today, settled with daily margin, and FUT shows the most active months across markets.

lessons.title: Futures curves and rolling (CTM)
lessons.summary: A futures curve lines up every contract month of one commodity, rising (contango) when storing costs money and falling (backwardation) when it is scarce now, and CTM shows it with the cost of rolling.

lessons.title: Who holds the futures (COT)
lessons.summary: The CFTC's weekly Commitments of Traders shows how many futures contracts speculators, hedgers and small traders hold long and short, and COT shows it per market with history and percentiles.

lessons.title: Oil and gas inventories (DOE, NGS)
lessons.summary: DOE and NGS show the weekly US government counts of crude, products and natural gas in storage against last year and the five-year range.

lessons.title: Power and the grid (POWER)
lessons.summary: POWER collects the public queues of power projects and large electricity users waiting to connect to the grid, with their history and outcomes.

lessons.title: GPU rental prices (GPU)
lessons.summary: GPU collects published hourly rental prices for AI chips by model and price basis, with list indexes, medians and history, so compute can be tracked like a commodity.

lessons.title: How a stock reacts on macro days (MDAY)
lessons.summary: MDAY compares how a US listing moves on CPI, jobs and Fed decision days with a normal day, over up to five years, and lists every release day with its move.

lessons.title: The yield curve and its spreads (GC)
lessons.summary: GC draws government yield curves for the US (nominal and real), Germany, the UK, Japan, Canada and the euro AAA curve, with the main slope spreads and their changes.

lessons.title: The Fed path (WIRP)
lessons.summary: WIRP turns the prices of overnight-rate futures into the rate the market expects after each scheduled Fed meeting, with hike or cut probabilities and the Fed's own projections.

lessons.title: Central bank rates around the world (CBR)
lessons.summary: CBR lists the policy rates of the G20 central banks, the SNB, Norges Bank, the Riksbank and the RBNZ with the current level, the last move and its date, and where each rate sits in its past year.

lessons.title: Money markets and liquidity (BTMM)
lessons.summary: BTMM shows where banks, funds and the government borrow for a night to a year: overnight rates, the Treasury bill curve, and the Fed's balance-sheet liquidity.

lessons.title: Treasury auctions (AUCT)
lessons.summary: AUCT lists upcoming and recent US Treasury auctions with the rate each cleared at, how well it was covered and who bought.

lessons.title: Pricing one bond (YAS)
lessons.summary: YAS is a bond calculator that turns a yield into a price (or back) and adds accrued interest, duration, convexity, DV01 and the spread to the Treasury curve.

lessons.title: Credit spreads (CRD)
lessons.summary: A credit spread is the extra yield a company pays over a government bond for the risk of not paying back, and CRD shows the spreads of US corporate bond indices by rating.

lessons.title: Credit default swaps (CDS, CDX, SOVR)
lessons.summary: A credit default swap is insurance on a borrower's default, and CDS, CDX and SOVR show reported trades on companies, the main indices and 5-year country spreads.

lessons.title: Debt maturities and covenants (DDIS, CRDOC, COVN)
lessons.summary: DDIS shows how much of a company's debt comes due each year, and CRDOC and COVN read its loan and bond documents into a capital structure and covenant headroom.

lessons.title: The economic calendar (ECO)
lessons.summary: ECO lists upcoming and recent economic releases and central bank events by time, with their impact and the actual, forecast and prior numbers.

lessons.title: Economic statistics (ECST)
lessons.summary: ECST is a dashboard of the main US economic statistics (inflation, labor, growth, housing, rates), each with its latest value and a chart against its own history.

lessons.title: Inflation by component (CPI)
lessons.summary: CPI breaks US consumer prices into their components with each one's weight, its monthly, annualized and yearly change, and its contribution to the headline.

lessons.title: Currencies and cross rates (FXC)
lessons.summary: FXC is a matrix of exchange rates between the major currencies, each cell saying how many units of the column currency one unit of the row currency buys.

lessons.title: World indices and trading hours (WEI, MAP)
lessons.summary: WEI lists the main stock indices of the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific with their level, change and session status, and MAP shows every trading venue on a world map.

lessons.title: Sectors, themes and rotation (BI, THEM, RRG)
lessons.summary: BI shows sector and industry performance, THEM curated themes as equal-weight baskets with breadth, and RRG plots each sector's strength and momentum against the market.
lessons.chapter: The big picture: macro, markets and news

lessons.title: The market heatmap (HM)
lessons.summary: HM draws the largest US stocks as rectangles sized by market value and colored by today's change.
lessons.chapter: The big picture: macro, markets and news

lessons.title: Movers, new highs and lows, halts (MOST, HILO, HALT)
lessons.summary: MOST lists today's biggest gainers, losers and most active stocks, HILO counts new session highs and lows live, and HALT lists trading halts.
lessons.chapter: The big picture: macro, markets and news

lessons.title: IPOs (IPO)
lessons.summary: IPO lists upcoming, priced and recent initial public offerings on the main US, Asia-Pacific and European venues, with size, price range and first-day performance.

lessons.title: Sentiment and market valuation (FNG, VAL)
lessons.summary: FNG shows a fear-and-greed gauge built from seven market signals, and VAL shows whole-market valuation ratios against their own history.

lessons.title: The news feeds (TOP, N, CN, NI, FIRST)
lessons.summary: Gloom shows one stream of stories five ways: TOP ranks what matters, N shows everything as it arrives, CN filters a company, NI a topic, and FIRST only breaking news.

lessons.title: Social posts, newsletters, TV and tech news (TWIT, SUB, TV, HN)
lessons.summary: Four optional panes bring outside media next to your data: TWIT (a live X search), SUB (your newsletters), TV (live business TV) and HN (Hacker News).
lessons.chapter: The big picture: macro, markets and news

lessons.title: Crypto from zero (CRYP)
lessons.summary: Crypto coins are digital assets recorded on public ledgers and traded around the clock on many venues, and CRYP lists the largest by market cap with price and changes.

lessons.title: Perpetual futures, funding and open interest (PERP)
lessons.summary: A perpetual future never expires and is kept close to its underlying by a periodic funding payment, and PERP shows a market's funding, open interest and premium over time.

lessons.title: Prediction markets (PM)
lessons.summary: In a prediction market a contract pays 1 dollar if an event happens and 0 if not, so its price in cents reads as the crowd's probability, and PM lists these markets by topic.

lessons.title: Political polls (POLL)
lessons.summary: POLL lists US political polls by type with date, subject, pollster, sample and result, and opens each one with its margin of error and the running average.

lessons.title: Drug safety reports and clinical trials (FDA, TRIAL)
lessons.summary: FDA searches public US reports of drug and device side effects and drug recalls, and TRIAL searches the public registry of clinical studies.

lessons.title: Litigation and SEC comment letters (LITI, CLTR)
lessons.summary: LITI lists a company's lawsuits, enforcement and antitrust cases with their documents and dated status, and CLTR lists the letters SEC staff sent the company about its filings and the replies.

lessons.title: Government contracts and awards (AWARDS)
lessons.summary: AWARDS collects published government contracts from the US, Europe, the UK and elsewhere, matches recipients to listed companies, and shows each award with its value and evidence.

lessons.title: Hiring signals (JOBS, HIRE)
lessons.summary: JOBS reads one company's open roles over time from its own careers site, and HIRE compares hiring momentum across companies.

lessons.title: App store rankings (APPS)
lessons.summary: APPS tracks where a listed company's apps rank on public app-store charts by country and chart, with ratings and an overall attention score.

lessons.title: Supply chains and scenario exposure (SPLC, EXPO)
lessons.summary: SPLC maps a company's customers, suppliers, competitors and investees from filings, announcements and calls with evidence, and EXPO estimates a portfolio's exposure to a shock along those links.

lessons.title: The AI infrastructure map (TBO)
lessons.summary: TBO opens a partner's research database on the physical build-out of AI and semiconductors: curated lists of companies by niche, physical sites, and dated research notes.

lessons.title: Searching calls, news and filings (SRCH)
lessons.summary: SRCH searches earnings-call transcripts, news and SEC filings at once and shows every passage that matches your phrase, with saved searches that alert you to new matches.
